title: Stop charging twice when the host is slow

blocks.text: Merchants complain that on slow days some cardholders are charged twice. The culprit is `PaymentClient.send` in `src/main/java/com/example/practice/PaymentClient.java`: when the host doesn't answer in time, it sends the same message again.

`send` handles every kind of message the client sends: purchases and authorizations, advices, and echoes. Fix the three places marked `TODO` so that each ends safely and returns the `Outcome` that says what happened:

items: `onNoAnswer`: when it didn't. This is the part that matters.

blocks.text: Anything that must still reach the host later goes onto the `saf.host` queue of the space (`sp.out`). Something else delivers it, as in 12.7. The `ReversalBuilder` from 12.6 is already in the file. About 15 lines in total.

cases.says: an answered purchase with 39=00 is approved and leaves nothing to send
an answer whose field 39 is not 00 is a decline, and a decline needs no reversal
a purchase with no answer goes to the host once and is reversed, never resent
the reversal is a new message with its own STAN that points at the original through field 90
an advice with no answer reports something that already happened, so it is queued to be repeated rather than reversed
a network message with no answer moved no money, so nothing is queued or resent
with the link down nothing is sent, so nothing needs reversing

origin.section: 12.5 No Answer Means You Don't Know

concepts: A reversal is a new message with its own STAN that points at the original through field 90.
With no answer the outcome is unknown: purchases are reversed and never resent, advices are repeated, network messages need nothing, and what never went out needs nothing.
